newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plate Glass eyes new offshore markets.
newsitem.headline: Plate Glass eyes new offshore markets.

text.p: South African glass manufacturer Plate Glass & Shatterprufe Industries Ltd said on Wednesday the time was ripe to start developing new markets for its offshore division, Belron International.

Ronnie Lubner, the chairman and chief executive officer of Plate Glass, said in the group's annual report that the proposed markets would be located close to existing operations and have substantial vehicle populations.

"This strategic shift is motivated by our desire to remain the world's largest automotive glass repair and replacement network and a recognition that, in our more established markets, competition is increasing as traditional participants aspire to protect their position," Lubner said.
To this end the group last month announced it had bought a leading Canadian retail glass business, Standard Auto Glass, for 120 million rand.

Lubner said a potential partner had been identified in India which although it has a relatively small per capita vehicle population, presents opportunities for growth over time, particularly in respect of automotive glass repairs.
Belron had also recently entered the Brazilian market which would provide a base for expansion to other parts of South America.
Following a tough year in the South African market, the Plate Glass group, which saw earnings slide to 702.0 cents a share from 745.0 cents, expected a better performance in the 1997/98 year.

"With the progressive resolution of manufacturing problems and expectations of a further improvement from Belron, a return to growth in earnings is anticipated, barring any deterioration in domestic demand," he said.

Sales at Belron, which operates primarily in the automotive repair and replacement glass market, were more than one billion dollars in the year to end-March and contributed a bulky 56.2 percent to the Plate Glass group's attributable income.
Belron has businesses in 13 countries structured into four regions, namely the USA, continental Europe, Australasia and the United Kingdom and Ireland.
